extracted.intended_audience: users and developers of computer algebra systems: computational algebraists, algebraic geometers, singularity theorists, and researchers seeking a CAS for polynomial computations
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or choosing a computer algebra system (Singular) for polynomial computations, algebraic geometry, and singularity theory based on features, algorithms, extensibility, documentation, licensing, and developer support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly efficient core algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular provides highly efficient core algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core algorithms handle Gröbner/standard bases and free resolutions, polynomial factorization, resultants, characteristic sets, and numerical root finding. Use this criterion to judge speed and reliability of fundamental computations required in commutative and non-commutative algebra tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of advanced algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular contains a multitude of advanced algorithms in the target fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are currently more than 90 libraries addressing topics such as absolute factorization, algebraic D-modules, classification of singularities, deformation theory, Gauss–Manin systems, Hamburger–Noether (Puiseux) development, invariant theory, (non-)commutative homological algebra, normalization, primary decomposition, resolution of singularities, and sheaf cohomology. Evaluate whether the needed specialized algorithms are present in these libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intuitive, C-like programming language
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular offers an intuitive, C-like programming language for scripting and customization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ease-of-use for writing procedures, implementing algorithms, and automating workflows; familiarity with C-like syntax may reduce the learning curve for users with programming experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensibility via user libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular provides easy ways to make it user-extendible through libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can write and add libraries to extend functionality. Consider how straightforward it is to develop, distribute, and integrate custom libraries for specific research needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive documentation and help
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular has a comprehensive online manual and help function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good documentation and in-program help support usability, onboarding, and reproducibility. Use this to judge how quickly new users can learn the system and how easy it is to find authoritative references for functions and options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for relevant computational objects and baserings
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular's main computational objects are ideals, modules and matrices over a large number of baserings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported baserings include polynomial rings over various ground fields and some rings (including the integers), localizations, a general class of non-commutative algebras (e.g., exterior algebra and the Weyl algebra), quotient rings, and tensor products. Evaluate whether the software supports the algebraic structures required by your problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with third-party software
rubrics_metrics.description: Further functionality is obtained by combining Singular with third-party software linked to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party integrations add tools for convex geometry, tropical geometry, and visualization. Consider availability and quality of external tool links when needing specialized geometry or plotting features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-source licensing (GNU GPL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular is free and open-source under the GNU General Public Licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing affects redistribution, modification, and use in commercial or collaborative projects. Use this criterion to determine legal/organizational suitability and whether source access meets reproducibility and extensibility goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active development and institutional backing
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular is developed by a core team (Wolfram Decker, Gert‑Martin Greuel, Gerhard Pfister, Hans Schönemann) within the Department of Mathematics at the University of Kaiserslautern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the presence of an active, named development team and institutional affiliation as indicators of ongoing maintenance, credibility, and community support.
